title: Resume a run after the person signed in
description: Resume a run paused on a sign-in or verification wall (pause.kind auth, waitingOn person, of dsagent.execution.wait) after the person told you they passed it.
guidance: Sign-in walls are the person's: ask them to sign in on the paused page (pause.pageContextId) and wait for them; never sign in, type, click or accept anything there yourself. The Extension reads the paused page again and resumes the run, as the person's Resume on the sign-in sheet does, only when no wall stands there: with the wall still present it refuses (TARGET_BUSY, businessCode AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED) and the run stays paused. A run usually resumes by itself a few seconds after the wall is gone, so a refusal with AUTH_PAUSE_NOT_OPEN often means it already did: follow it with dsagent.execution.wait. Only the agent that started the run may resume it (after a restart of your Connector pass runToken). The pause's deadline is unchanged. Requires an idempotency key.

executionId.description: The paused run, as dsagent.execution.run or dsagent.wizard.run returned it.

runToken.description: The run's ownership token, as dsagent.execution.run or dsagent.wizard.run returned it (shown once). Pass it when your browser connection was renewed (a restarted Connector): the run, its open repair handoff and its pages follow you to the new connection. Not needed on the connection that started the run.

executionId.description: The run, running again; follow it with dsagent.execution.wait.

resumed.description: Always true: the wall was checked gone and the run resumed.
